claims.text: The Ru fraction strongly governs the rate of carbonaceous-intermediate oxidation in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs ethanol-oxidation catalysts.
Reducing the Ru content diminishes Ru's synergistic promotion of water activation.
Diminished water activation causes greater accumulation of carbonaceous intermediates.
Greater accumulation of carbonaceous intermediates lowers ethanol-oxidation activity.
Greater accumulation of carbonaceous intermediates decreases catalyst durability.
Increasing the Ru content enhances water activation at the alloy surface.
Enhanced water activation facilitates oxidative removal of adsorbed carbonaceous species.
Ru–OH sites form more readily at higher Ru content.
Ru–OH sites accelerate oxidation of poisoning intermediates such as adsorbed CO.
Accelerated oxidation of poisoning intermediates improves ethanol-oxidation activity and stability.
Relative to the baseline, reduced-Ru catalysts will have lower current densities.
Relative to the baseline, reduced-Ru catalysts will undergo faster performance decay.
Relative to the baseline, increased-Ru catalysts will have improved kinetic metrics.
Relative to the baseline, increased-Ru catalysts will deactivate more slowly.
The proposed Ru-mediated mechanism should dominate from 0.3 to 0.8 V versus RHE and 25 to 80 °C in acidic or alkaline electrolyte.
Adsorbed carbonaceous intermediates form and require oxidative removal within the stated ethanol-electrooxidation operating range.
Ru content can be varied while total metal loading and the relative proportions of the other metals are held constant.
The optimum Ru loading and magnitude of performance enhancement may depend on interactions with the other alloy components and on electrolyte conditions.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires constant total metal loading while Ru content changes and the other-metal ratios remain fixed, which requires adjustment of their absolute amounts. The falsification design instead says to maintain identical loadings of all other metals; changing Ru under that constraint changes total metal loading.
